views.name: 2. bars: best mean time in sf
views.sql:
-- Best (minimum) observed time for each engine x query x machine.
-- Most of this is to parse the json in the cmake_defs col.
-- adjust sf and or remove threads filters to make this query have a lot more data.

WITH best AS (
  SELECT node, query, q_number, engine,
         build_event_id, config_name, head, cmake_defs,
         ROUND(MIN(mean_ms), 3) AS best_ms,   -- keep this the ONLY min/max here
         COUNT(*)               AS runs_considered
  FROM v_runs
  WHERE quality = 'clean'
    AND sf_label = 'sf1'
    AND threads  = 1
    AND q_number <> 5          -- q5 excluded; delete this line to include it
    AND mean_ms IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY node, q_number, engine
)
SELECT node, query, q_number, engine,
       build_event_id, config_name, head,
       best_ms, runs_considered,
       COALESCE((
         SELECT group_concat(label, ', ')
         FROM (
           SELECT CASE WHEN upper(j.value) = 'ON' THEN j.key
                       ELSE j.key || '=' || j.value END AS label
           FROM json_each(best.cmake_defs) j
           WHERE upper(COALESCE(j.value, '')) NOT IN ('OFF','FALSE','NO','0','')
           ORDER BY j.key
         )
       ), 'none (baseline)') AS flags_on
FROM best
ORDER BY node, q_number, engine

views.name: 4. scaling curves (2^k only)
views.sql:
-- Log-log scaling. A straight line of slope -1 is perfect scaling;
-- flattening is where adding threads stops paying.
--
-- GROUPING: every non-aggregate column in the SELECT is also in the GROUP BY.
-- SQLite allows a bare column in an aggregate query and just picks an
-- arbitrary row for it, so dropping one silently AVERAGES its series together
-- and mislabels the result. That is how you get one line per engine when you
-- expected one per (engine, build, scale factor).
--
-- Restricted to power-of-two thread counts via (threads & (threads-1)) = 0,
-- which is true only when exactly one bit is set. Drop that line to include
-- every measured thread count.
SELECT m.stable_key AS node,
       q.label      AS query,
       q.q_number,
       e.code       AS engine,
       bs.config_name,
       d.sf_label,
       be.build_event_id,
       t.threads,
       ROUND(AVG(r.median_ns) / 1e6, 3) AS median_ms,
       COUNT(*)                         AS n_runs
FROM run r
JOIN task t              ON t.task_id = r.task_id
JOIN query q             ON q.query_id = t.query_id
JOIN dataset d           ON d.dataset_id = t.dataset_id
JOIN engine e            ON e.engine_id = r.engine_id
JOIN build_event be      ON be.build_event_id = r.build_event_id
JOIN build_spec bs       ON bs.spec_id = be.spec_id
JOIN machine_snapshot ms ON ms.snapshot_id = r.snapshot_id
JOIN machine m           ON m.machine_id = ms.machine_id
WHERE r.quality = 'clean'
  AND (t.threads & (t.threads - 1)) = 0     -- powers of two only
  AND q.q_number <> 5          -- q5 excluded; delete this line to include it
  -- AND bs.config_name = 'default_huge'
  -- AND d.sf_label = 'sf10'
GROUP BY m.machine_id, q.query_id, e.engine_id,
         be.build_event_id, d.dataset_id, t.threads
ORDER BY m.stable_key, q.q_number, t.threads

views.name: all runs
views.sql:
SELECT * FROM v_runs
ORDER BY node, config_name, sf_label, query, threads, engine

views.name: counters
views.sql:
-- Raw counters, one row per run. Within a single vendor only: ARM's nearest
-- LLC-miss event does not count what Intel's counts. Use the
-- 'counters cross-vendor' view when spanning burrata and an x86 node.
SELECT * FROM v_run_counters_wide
ORDER BY config_name, sf_label, query, threads

views.name: counters cross-vendor
views.sql:
-- Only counters that mean the same thing on ARM and x86.
SELECT r.node, r.config_name, r.sf_label, r.query, r.engine, r.threads,
       r.median_ms,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.event='cycles'       THEN c.value END) AS cycles,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.event='instructions' THEN c.value END) AS instructions,
       MAX(CASE WHEN c.event='task_clock'   THEN c.value END) AS task_clock,
       ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN c.event='instructions' THEN c.value END) /
             NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN c.event='cycles' THEN c.value END),0), 3) AS ipc
FROM v_runs r
JOIN v_counters_comparable c ON c.run_id = r.run_id
GROUP BY r.run_id
ORDER BY r.node, r.query, r.threads

views.name: machines
views.sql:
SELECT m.stable_key AS node, m.partition, ms.snapshot_id,
       ms.cpu_vendor, ms.cpu_model, ms.cores_physical, ms.threads_logical,
       ms.numa_nodes, ms.l3_bytes, ms.kernel_version, ms.observed_from
FROM machine_snapshot ms
JOIN machine m ON m.machine_id = ms.machine_id
ORDER BY node, ms.observed_from DESC

views.name: builds
views.sql:
SELECT be.build_event_id, bs.config_name,
       substr(hex(bs.repo_sha),1,8) AS head, bs.repo_dirty, bs.cmake_defs,
       substr(hex(b.content_sha256),1,12) AS binary_sha, be.built_at
FROM build_event be
JOIN build_spec bs ON bs.spec_id = be.spec_id
JOIN binary b      ON b.binary_id = be.binary_id
ORDER BY be.built_at DESC

views.name: headers
views.sql:
-- Counter columns each header layout supplies. burrata's PMU exposes fewer
-- events, so its .out is narrower than v4's.
SELECT * FROM v_header_expectations ORDER BY header_version

views.name: reproducibility
views.sql:
-- Same recipe, same commit, different bits: cross-build deltas may be
-- codegen luck rather than signal.
SELECT * FROM spec_reproducibility

views.name: schema
views.sql:
SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master
WHERE name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY type, name

views.name: best time by engine
views.sql:
-- Best (minimum) mean time per machine, query and engine. Typer and
-- Tectorwise are the cmake_defaults builds; Otherwise is every fair_best
-- build of the vectorized engine.
SELECT node, query, q_number,
       CASE WHEN engine = 'h' THEN 'Typer'
            WHEN config_name LIKE 'cmake_defaults%' THEN 'Tectorwise'
            ELSE 'Otherwise' END AS system,
       ROUND(MIN(mean_ms), 3) AS best_ms,
       COUNT(*)               AS runs_considered
FROM v_runs
WHERE quality = 'clean'
  AND sf_label = 'sf1'
  AND threads  = 1
  AND q_number <> 5
  AND mean_ms IS NOT NULL
  AND (config_name LIKE 'cmake_defaults%'
       OR (engine = 'v' AND config_name LIKE 'fair_best%'))
GROUP BY node, q_number, system
ORDER BY node, q_number, system

views.name: operator families
views.sql:
SELECT machine, sf, query, query_order,
       CASE f.build WHEN 'VW:cmake_defaults' THEN 'VW' ELSE f.build END AS build,
       build_short,
       build_order, family, family_order, ms, pct, run_ms, solid
FROM fig_operator_families f
WHERE f.sf = 1
  AND f.build NOT IN ('VW:par_crc32', 'Typer@HEAD', 'VW:jd_all_pc')
  AND f.query <> 'Q5'
views.desc: Single-threaded runtime per TPC-H query and build at SF 1, split by operator family from Linux perf sampling. T = Typer, TW = Tectorwise and VW = a minimally modernized version of Tectorwise. Typer is not split by operator.

views.name: vtune stalls
views.sql:
SELECT machine, sf, query, query_label,
       CASE f.build WHEN 'VW:cmake_defaults' THEN 'VW' ELSE f.build END AS build,
       build_short,
       build_order, category, category_order, is_stall, value_ms, pct_of_stall,
       stall_ms, total_ms
FROM fig_vtune_breakdown f
WHERE f.sf = 1
  AND f.build NOT IN ('Typer@HEAD', 'VW:jd_all_pc')
  AND f.query <> 5
views.desc: Cycles per TPC-H query and build at SF 1 from VTune: retiring (useful work) plus the Sirin and Ailamaki stall categories. Show switches between share of runtime, share of stall time (retiring hidden) and milliseconds.

views.name: stalls per operator
views.sql:
SELECT machine, stall_model, sf, query, query_order,
       CASE f.build WHEN 'VW:cmake_defaults' THEN 'VW' ELSE f.build END AS build,
       build_order, build_ms, op_order, operator, op_family, op_label, op_ms,
       op_share, category, category_key, category_order, frac, ms
FROM fig_stalls_per_operator f
WHERE f.sf = 1
  AND f.build NOT IN ('Typer@HEAD', 'VW:jd_all_pc')
  AND f.query <> 'Q5'
views.desc: For one TPC-H query at SF 1: each operator's runtime (its share of perf-sampled cycles times the untraced runtime), split by top-down stall category and grouped by build. The categories depend on what each machine's performance counters can measure. Operators under 1.5% of the run are merged.
